solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Comic actor means well, I think, when performing

indicators.note: the letters are put through their paces, acted out in a new order

explanation.surface: A comedian on stage is generously credited with good intentions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when performing' signals that MEANS WELL I THINK is rearranged; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Williams was a celebrated British comedy actor of the Carry On films and radio's Round the Horne.

clue.text: Beginning to go mad

definitions.meaning: the start of something, as of a football match
informal British for erupting in anger or trouble

explanation.surface: Someone starting to lose their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the start of a match and, in British slang, becoming furious or violent.

clue.text: Group's lack of connection to World Wide Web

parts.note: lack of something means there is none: no
the internet is often called the net

explanation.surface: A complaint that a band or organisation has no internet access.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine performers or nine items is a musical term for a set of nine.

clue.text: Environmental markers local bees swarm round

indicators.note: bees that swarm round fly about in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Neighbourhood bees buzz about green labels on products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swarm round' signals that LOCAL BEES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Eco-labels are product tags certifying environmental friendliness, so they mark goods for green credentials.

clue.text: Actors having bit of a laugh over script

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: ha is one burst of laughter
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a handwritten script

explanation.surface: Performers chuckling as they look over their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places HA above MS in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Overacting performers are called hams, a derogatory word for theatrical players.

clue.text: Vessel a waitress overturned in pub

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: in a down light, overturned means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a maid can be a serving girl

explanation.surface: A boat — or a jug — knocked over by a server in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses A MAID to DIAMA, which goes 'in' INN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a large merchant sailing ship trading with India, so a type of vessel.

clue.text: Secondary school leads in learning: you can expect excellence

indicators.note: leads are the front letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A school's promise: where you learn, you'll find excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads in' takes the first letters of learning, you, can, expect, excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: A French state secondary school is called a lycée.

clue.text: Mugger picked up a book in church?

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio, meaning heard rather than seen

parts.note: a psalter is a book of psalms used in church

explanation.surface: A thief who grabs a hymnbook from a pew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' signals a word heard: A PSALTER, said aloud, matches the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugger attacks people in the street, so is one who commits physical attacks.

clue.text: Queen, perhaps, taken to new liquor store?

parts.note: a queen bee is an example of a female bee, a she-bee

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the monarch has been brought to a newly opened off-licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks royal, but with 'perhaps' it is the hive's female bee.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, especially in Ireland or South Africa, where illicit liquor is sold.

clue.text: New group of pupils in school followed rules

indicators.note: the new class goes inside the word for school

parts.note: a co-ed is a mixed school
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A fresh class at school obediently kept to the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: A co-ed is a school taking both boys and girls; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply with rules or standards, so the past tense means obeyed them.

clue.text: Class sets actually reduced in size, on reflection

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so the letters run backwards
only part of the phrase sets actually is kept, a smaller piece of it

explanation.surface: School sets have truly shrunk, someone muses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced in size' takes ETSAC from inside 'sets actually'; 'on reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social rank, a class of society.

clue.text: Unusually big bird, bony

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for unusually big sizes
a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: An oversized bird turns out to be all skin and bone.
explanation.walkthrough: OS, for outsize, is a British clothing label.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is a technical adjective meaning relating to or resembling bone.

clue.text: Breed of dog — not bitch — unable to bark?

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog, so a dog that is not one is male
a dog that cannot bark is mute

explanation.surface: Asking whether a dog breed is a silent male.
explanation.definitionFit: The malemute (malamute) is an Alaskan sled dog breed.

clue.text: Join person starving shortly before noon

indicators.note: cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: someone going without food is a faster

explanation.surface: Someone hungry meets up just before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts the last letter from FASTER, giving FASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten is to attach or fix together, so to join.

clue.text: Item of furniture manufactured in Leeds (GB)

indicators.note: made up, so the letters are assembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture made in the Yorkshire city, Great Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges IN LEEDS GB; Leeds is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed for one person is a piece of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: Russian who gained power when installed by tsar ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
something installed has been put in

explanation.surface: A Russian leader rose to power once installed by the tsar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian who gained power' tempts a modern president, half of the answer's letters, but the whole is the def; 'ultimately' takes the last letter of tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin was the Siberian mystic who gained great influence at the Romanov court.

clue.text: At the moment very little money gets moved into bank

parts.note: P stands for penny, a tiny sum

indicators.note: the word for moved goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
something moved has been sent

explanation.surface: A tiny sum is now being transferred into an account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial but is the verb, as in 'bank on'; 'into' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Presently can mean now, currently, especially in American and Scottish usage.

clue.text: Archdeacon 'aving 'eadgear, up for a fight

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

indicators.note: in a down light, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: having headgear is hatted; dropping the H as the clue does gives atted

explanation.surface: A Cockney-voiced clergyman in a hat, spoiling for a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped aitches tell you to drop the H from HATTED; 'up' reverses ATTED to DETTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud, a bitter fight between parties.

clue.text: Container of cold wine knocked back

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: knocked back as a drink is, but here meaning the letters go backwards

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

explanation.surface: A tin of chilled wine downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses RETSINA to ANISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a round metal container, such as for tea.

clue.text: One employed by theatre company welcomes everyone — bravo!

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so these go inside

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for company
everyone means all
Bravo is B in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe hails everybody with cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' puts ALL B inside COY, the army abbreviation for company.
explanation.definitionFit: A callboy summons actors to the stage when their cue is due, a theatre job.

clue.text: Hard to connect electrical supply in home

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to earth a circuit is to connect it to ground

explanation.surface: Struggling to get electricity wired up in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'earth' is the ground connection of a circuit, called ground in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for the household, as in 'hearth and home'.

clue.text: Fellow eats scrap, deprived of starter before a meal?

indicators.note: eats means swallows, so the fellow's two letters take the trimmed scrap inside them

parts.note: a fellow is a he

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a scrap is a fight

explanation.surface: A man tucks into leftovers without a first course before dining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of starter' drops a first letter, leaving IGHT; 'eats' is the containment signal. 'Scrap' and 'starter' play on food.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is an early evening meal with cooked food in Britain.

clue.text: A way to get in money for religious movement

indicators.note: the letters are placed inside the slang word for cash

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A method of raking in cash for a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for cash; 'to get in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollardy was the movement of Wycliffe's followers in medieval England.

clue.text: Athenian character's surprised expression, carrying revolver

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside

parts.note: aha is an exclamation of surprise
an LP record spins on a turntable

explanation.surface: An Athenian gasps on finding someone armed with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' suggests a gun but is a record that revolves; 'carrying' puts LP in AHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, a character Athenians wrote.

clue.text: Sailor, say, goes on ship's prow without fuss

indicators.note: goes on means follows after the first piece
the prow is the front, so the opening letter
without means outside, so one goes round the other

parts.note: e.g. means for example, say
ado is fuss

explanation.surface: A seaman, for instance, boards at the bow quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking; 'goes on' sets the result after the prow letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, experienced sailor is called a sea dog.

clue.text: Fear money is short after onset of devaluation

indicators.note: the cut slang word comes after the first letter
the onset is the first letter
money that is short is lacking a bit, so the slang word loses its final letter

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: Anxiety about running out of cash once the currency is devalued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for cash; 'is short' trims it, and 'after' sets it behind the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension.

clue.text: Repair minute object

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Fixing a tiny item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' reads as tiny but is the time unit, M.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend is to fix or repair something.

clue.text: The BBC broadcast musical work, a form of jazz

indicators.note: broadcast means heard over the air, so the sound counts

parts.note: the Beeb is the nickname for the BBC
op. is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: The BBC airs a piece of music in a jazz style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' means the Beeb's sound, not its spelling, gives the first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is a fast, complex style of jazz from the 1940s.

clue.text: Something for nothing: half of my ear, nose and throat surgery

parts.note: a treat is something given free

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word, its first letter

parts.note: ENT is the hospital department for ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: Free surgery on my ear, nose and throat — half of it, anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes M from 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery is a form of medical care given to a patient.

clue.text: Talk, repeatedly recalling a significant WW2 date

indicators.note: repeatedly means the reversed piece is written again and again
recalling means calling back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: D-Day, 6 June 1944, was the Normandy landings
the same date, a D-Day, recalled once more for the third run

explanation.surface: Chatting endlessly about remembering an important wartime date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' turns A D-DAY backwards; 'repeatedly' has it written out three times in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is dismissive slang for tedious chatter, like 'blah blah blah'.
